findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — The light-theme value was changed, not just the dark value added: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. In light themes this bold link now renders as very light gray on a white background (poor contrast/readability). Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:~522 — `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness, making it identical to the adjacent `.title` rule and inconsistent with `common/base/user.scss`, which correctly keeps 30%/70% for `.name`. Looks like a copy-paste from the neighboring `.title` line; light-theme appearance regresses.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:~497 — Same copy-paste error as desktop: `.name` light value changed 30% → 50%, diverging from `common/base/user.scss` (30%) and collapsing the visual distinction between `.name` and `.title` in light themes.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:~182 — Topic-map `h3` light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness. The equivalent rule in `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly keeps 20%/80%, so mobile light themes now render this heading much lighter than desktop (washed-out heading, reduced contrast).

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:~102 — `.custom-message-length` light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness (values effectively swapped). The identical rule in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly keeps 70% light / 30% dark, so mobile light themes now render this hint text far darker than desktop.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:~522 — `.name` light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness, making it identical to the adjacent `.title` rule and inconsistent with `common/base/user.scss`, which correctly keeps 30%/70% for `.name`. adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss, the `.name` rule under the user header block changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, which makes the light-theme value 50% lightness—matching the adjacent `.title` rule (also 50%/50%). This is inconsistent with common/base/user.scss where `.name` remains `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, supporting the finding that the desktop light-theme appearance likely regresses due to a copy/paste error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:~497 — Same copy-paste error as desktop: `.name` light value changed 30% → 50%, diverging from `common/base/user.scss` (30%) and collapsing the visual distinction between `.name` and `.title` in light themes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss`, the diff changes `.name` from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, while `.title` in the same block is also set to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. This makes `.name` and `.title` identical in light mode (both 50% lightness), unlike `common/base/user.scss` where `.name` uses 30% lightness, so the finding’s “30% → 50% collapsing distinction” is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the `a.star h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which makes the light-theme heading substantially lighter. In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`, the equivalent `a.star h3` rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, preserving the stronger contrast in light theme. The diff therefore shows a real, introduced inconsistency likely causing washed-out headings on mobile light themes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` is changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which makes the light-theme branch use 30% lightness (darker) and the dark-theme branch use 70% (lighter). The corresponding rule in `desktop/modal.scss` uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so mobile is inconsistent and appears to have the light/dark values swapped.
